items.title: Nilekani Proposes Last-Minute AI-Assembled Exams To Stop Paper Leaks In India
items.summary: Following widespread public outcry and systemic disruptions caused by national exam paper leaks, tech leader Nandan Nilekani proposed leveraging artificial intelligence to generate unique examination papers on the fly minutes before test execution. By assembling questions dynamically from a secure question bank, this model aims to eliminate traditional printing presses, transit logistics, and leak windows. However, implementing dynamic AI exam generation across millions of candidates introduces complex technical challenges regarding computer-adaptive testing (CAT), algorithmic difficulty normalization, hallucination risks, and regional language translation accuracy. In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Gaurav Lakhani (Co-Founder & COO, Voxturr / CEO, Vster) and Vivek Varshney (Founder, SpeedLabs India). They evaluate the feasibility of last-minute AI question generation versus pre-verified dynamic pools, Computer-Based Testing (CBT) security, auditing dynamic algorithms for difficulty parity, regional language translations, infrastructural recovery for rural testing centers, and building student trust through adaptive pilot benchmarks.
